introduction: Today, on the last Sunday of the liturgical year, we celebrate Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe. The tribes of Israel anoint David as their shepherd king. Paul sings of Christ, the image of the invisible God, in whom all things hold together. In the Gospel, Jesus reigns from the cross, and promises the repentant thief: Today you will be with me in Paradise. Let us ask Christ our King to remember us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Father has brought us into the Kingdom of his beloved Son. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim Christ as King by serving as he served. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who govern nations: that they may rule with justice and care for the weakest. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are dying, especially those who turn to God at the end of their lives: that they may hear Christ promise them Paradise. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prisoners and all who are condemned: that they may meet the mercy of Christ the King. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that Christ may reign in our hearts, and remember us in his Kingdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, you have given all things to your Son, the King who reigns from the cross. Remember us in his Kingdom, and make us faithful subjects of his love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Remember me
reflection.body:
On the last Sunday of the Church's year, we celebrate Christ the King. But the Gospel does not show us a throne of gold. It shows us Jesus on the cross.

The leaders mock him: "He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God." The soldiers mock him too: "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!" Above his head hangs a sign meant as an insult: "THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS." Yet the sign tells the truth. This is how Jesus reigns: not by saving himself, but by giving himself for others.

One of the criminals crucified beside him joins in the mockery. But the other rebukes him: "we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong." Then he turns to Jesus and makes a simple request: "Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom." Jesus answers, "Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise." The first person to enter Christ's Kingdom is a criminal who trusted him at the last moment.

The first reading recalls David being anointed king. The tribes remind him of God's words: "You will be shepherd of my people Israel." The true king is a shepherd.

Paul gives us a hymn to Christ's universal kingship. God "delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love." Christ "is the image of the invisible God," and "in him all things are held together." Through the cross he has reconciled everything to God, "having made peace through the blood of his cross."

As the year ends, make the good thief's prayer your own. Jesus, remember me. And let Christ reign in your heart, your home and your work.
